text:
maya: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can we get concrete GA windows for API, Console, and Optimize? people asked for dates to plan migrations. :calendar:
jordan: short answer: trying to avoid hard dates, but here's a working plan so teams can prep. i'll list current target windows and hard dependencies.
sam: +1, will call out infra blockers. key is GPU availability for dedicated tests.
leah: infra note: dedicated-capacity signoff depends on two infra items: (1) autoscaler stability (ETA ~2 weeks), (2) encryption-at-rest verification (ETA ~3 weeks). both must be green before GA.
tess: Console UX freeze: we need dev sign-off on the new routing UI before we ship. target freeze in 3 weeks, but if SDK changes happen earlier we might shift.
jordan: Targets (subject to the infra/dev blockers above):
- API (hosted): beta -> public GA window: mid-May to early June (approx).
- Console: feature-complete by end of May, GA in late June.
- Optimize (cost/perf toolkit): staged GA starting late June, broad GA mid-July.
These are windows not hard dates; i'll post an RFC with exact milestones.
ryan: migration docs ask: will we have a single migration guide for SDK v2 -> v3? if so, can we get a prerelease doc so customers can start early?
jordan: yes, we plan a single migration guide + quickstart. target draft in 1 week. release notes published with canary.
sam: engineering constraints: model-variant fallback and routing changes require a small runtime change that needs a canary (2-3 days) then a broader rollout. that pushes Console GA if UX depends on the runtime.
leah: deploy-bot scheduled canary for runtime change on 1938765560 (internal). will post status updates.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: runtime/fallbacks v1.2 -> canary start 1938765560, expected 48h, notify #eng-oncall for anomalies.
tess: for Console UX we can decouple some pieces (view-only vs. rollout controls) so we can ship view-only earlier if needed. that would let Console GA align closer to API GA.
maya: thanks — this is helpful. jordan, please make the RFC that clearly maps milestone -> dependency -> owner. teams need the doc to decide on cutting over.
jordan: will do. i'll create RFC + a short matrix and ping owners. expected RFC by EOD tomorrow. @ryan i'll put the draft migration guide link in the RFC.
ryan: perfect, thanks. i'll start drafting a migration checklist for customer comms and sample code snippets.
maya: one ask from leadership: pick the signal we use for 'GA readiness' (ops metrics + evals). prefer a small checklist: canary pass, perf within target, migration docs published, and support runbook ready.
sam: agreed. i'll own the perf metric and canary stability checks.
leah: i'll own infra verification + KMS checks.
jordan: putting owners in RFC. will include timeline table + fallback plan if infra misses dates.
maya: great — leaning on owners to be conservative on GA windows, but keep us informed if we can accelerate. :rocket:
ryan: will also prepare a short 'what to tell customers' blurb for comms.
jersey: (typo in participants list) — ignore
maya: haha noted. thanks everyone.
